title: Derived maps out of a perfect constant complex are locally algebraic
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site with final object $X$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and let $R$ be a commutative ring. Use constant sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and their derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $P,L\in D(R)$ with $P$ perfect, meaning that it is represented by a bounded complex of finitely generated projective $R$-modules [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. For every morphism $\varphi:\underline P\to\underline L$ in $D(\mathcal C,\underline R)$ there is a covering $\{U_i\to X\}$ and morphisms $\alpha_i:P\to L$ in $D(R)$ such that $\varphi|_{U_i}=\underline{\alpha_i}|_{U_i}$ in $D(\mathcal C/U_i,\underline R|_{U_i})$. Here restriction and the localized site are [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. No boundedness or finiteness is required of $L$, and the site need not have points.

source.place: Tag 09BE, lemma-locally-constant-map; exact statement, for a commutative coefficient ring.

proof.text: Choose the bounded finite-projective model F from perfectness and a complex model G of L from essential surjectivity of Q. Enlarge the two support bounds to min and max, so no ordered-bounds hypothesis is introduced. Use the exact constant functor localization comparison to transport the given map to a derived map between the constant complex models.
Apply the existing perfect-source local chain-representative theorem to obtain a covering and actual chain maps on each slice.

Apply the bounded finite constant-chain-map algebraicity theorem to each local representative. This gives further covering presieves and algebraic chain maps, with componentwise equality after further restriction.

Prove that overMap is exact by reflecting finite limits through the underlying additive sheaf functor and preserving local surjectivity. The composition and natural-isomorphism comparisons for exact derived functors identify iterated restriction with direct restriction. Localization naturality carries the componentwise chain equality to equality of the restricted derived maps. Define the algebraic derived map by transporting Q(b) along the model isomorphisms; factorization naturality proves that its constant realization is the desired map. Cancel the two model isomorphisms and compose the covering presieves using bind; reindex the composed presieve by its arrows.
